newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Feb industrial output plummets 7.39 pct.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Feb industrial output plummets 7.39 pct.

text.p: Colombia's industrial output in February, excluding coffee processing, fell a precipitous 7.39 percent compared with the same month a year ago, the National Statistics Department DANE said.

The fall, the worst on record in 15 years, underscored the depth of the recession that the government revealed for the first time Thursday, when the National Planning Department reported that Colombia's gross domestic product dropped for the second consecutive period in the first quarter of 1997.
DANE gave no specific reason for the sharp decline in manufacturing in February, which followed a 0.65 percent fall in January.
But the Planning Department, which reported that GDP fell 1.22 percent in the first quarter, said industrial output fell 2.6 percent for the quarter.
The Planning Department's figures were based on preliminary estimates for March. DANE's report on industrial performance in February was released after the overall GDP number for the first quarter.
According to DANE, industrial output excluding coffee processing fell by 4.53 in January and February and by 3.71 percent when coffee production is taken into account.
As measured over 12 months ending March 1, DANE said industrial production had fallen by 4.35 percent compared to the 12-month period ending March 1, 1996.

Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo conceded in an interview with local radio early Friday that the economy was showing "signs of recession," but he said it was important to remain optimistic and voiced his confidence that higher coffee prices and a trend toward lower domestic interest rates would spark a turnaround in the second half of the year.
"I even have the impression that figures for the second quarter are going to be very positive, but we'll have to wait to see the numbers," he said.
